wave: CORRECTNESS -- close a real fact-fabrication defect in STATE's self.field access model, found while checking its own documented single-level-only scope boundary
wave_title: Pivoting away from EffectCategory (per the immediately preceding generation's own note not to mine it indefinitely), this generation examined STATE's own documented scope boundary ('single-level self.field READ/WRITE extraction ... A nested chain like self.a.b reports a Read of self.a only'). Reading the actual code behind that boundary found it was not merely incomplete but WRONG: self.a.b used as a WRITE target fabricated a spurious Read of the outer field and never recorded the real write.
priority_classification: correctness / architectural integrity (priority 1) -- this is not new capability, it is fixing an existing capability that produces a wrong observable fact, discovered by reading the code behind an already-documented scope boundary rather than accepting the boundary's own framing ('reports a Read of self.a only') at face value.
how_the_defect_was_confirmed: Before writing any fix, extracted a minimal fixture (`self.a.b = 5;` inside a method) using the real, unmodified extractor and printed the raw StateAccessIdentity observations. Result: exactly one access, `name="a" kind=Read` -- confirming the WRITE target of an assignment was reported as a READ of the wrong (outer) field, and the real write was never recorded at all. This is the same falsify-the-baseline-first discipline used for every prior gap this session found (let-else, `?`, unsafe): confirm the actual current behavior directly, don't assume the documentation's own framing is complete or accurate.
root_cause: `self_field_ident` matched only the exact depth-1 shape `self.<field>` and returned `None` for anything deeper. For `self.a.b = x`, the assignment-target match arm's guard `self_field_ident(field).is_some()` failed (the outer field's base is `self.a`, an `Expr::Field`, not the required `Expr::Path` for a bare `self`), falling through to the arm's own `other => self.walk_expr(other)` fallback -- which re-dispatched the WHOLE `self.a.b` expression through the general `Expr::Field` READ-handling arm, where `self_field_ident` ALSO failed on the outer field but that arm's OWN fallback (`None => self.walk_expr(&field.base)`) walked into `self.a` alone, which DID match at that depth and emitted a Read.

design_decisions.question: Represent `self.a.b` as one compound event (joined path "a.b") or decompose into two events (Read of `a`, then Read/Write of `b`)?
design_decisions.decision: One compound event, joined by `.`. Rust's own place-expression semantics settle this: evaluating `self.a.b` (whether as a read or as a write target) computes `self.a` as a PLACE, never loads it as a VALUE, then projects `.b` from that place -- there is no separate 'read of self.a' event to report, at any depth. Decomposing into per-level events would fabricate an event Rust's own semantics do not produce, exactly the mistake the pre-existing single-level design already made once (by conflating 'the base needed walking for something else' with 'the base was itself accessed').

design_decisions.question: What should happen when a chain doesn't fully resolve (a tuple-index member anywhere, or a non-self root)?
design_decisions.decision: Discovered mid-fix, via the adversarial test for `self.field.0`: the naive fallback (`None => self.walk_expr(&field.base)`) reproduces the IDENTICAL fabrication bug one level down whenever `field.base` is itself another `Expr::Field` -- `self.field.0`'s outer (unnamed-tail) failure fell back to walking `self.field`, which DOES resolve, wrongly re-reporting a bare Read of `field` alone (the exact same defect class as the original bug, just surfacing at the boundary between a nameable prefix and an unnameable tail). Fixed by `walk_unresolved_field_base`: only recurse into the base when it is NOT itself an `Expr::Field` -- i.e. only when the base might hide a genuinely UNRELATED self-access (a call's argument, a method-call receiver's own sub-expressions, ...), never to re-attempt field-chain interpretation on a sub-chain the extractor already determined, as a whole, it cannot honestly name.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: self.a.b (any depth, any read/write/compound-assignment context) now produces exactly one correctly-kinded state-access event against the full joined path, with no fabricated partial-path event at any failure boundary, while still finding genuinely unrelated self-accesses buried in non-field sub-expressions.
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: Rewrote the prior generation's own baseline test (which had explicitly asserted the OLD single-level-only, and as it turns out WRONG-for-writes, behavior) to assert the correct joined-path Read. Added: a write-specific test proving no spurious Read accompanies the real Write; a three-level chain test; a tuple-index-anywhere-bails-the-chain test (both base and tail positions); a test for the second fabrication instance found mid-fix (`self.field.0`'s fallback), confirmed to fail before the `walk_unresolved_field_base` fix was written; and a test proving the fix does not OVER-suppress -- a genuinely unrelated self-access inside a call argument (`self.helper(self.value).z`) is still found.
stable_validator_law_compliance.independent_evidence_channel: cargo build --workspace clean. cargo fmt --all --check clean. cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean. Full cargo test --workspace: 277 adapter (+6 net, +1 rewritten), 2 apps/cli, 160 core, 63 runtime -- 502 total, 0 failed on the run that mattered (one intermediate run failed exactly as predicted on the tuple-index-tail case before the walk_unresolved_field_base fix was added, confirming that test was a real falsification, not a tautology). docs audit gate_ready: true. systemize against this repository's own real source: exit 0.
